domain_description: Comprehensive water rights and environmental analysis covering surface water and groundwater rights, permitting, water quality regulation, produced water management, and injection well operations. Focused on oil and gas industry water issues in Texas and the Permian Basin, grounded in the Clean Water Act, Safe Drinking Water Act, Texas Water Code, EPA regulations, and Railroad Commission of Texas rules.
authority_sources: EPA Underground Injection Control Regulations (40 CFR 144-148)
Railroad Commission of Texas Statewide Rules (16 TAC Chapter 3)
Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) Rules (30 TAC)
Texas Groundwater Conservation District Act (TWC Chapter 36)
EPA Clean Water Act Section 402 NPDES Regulations (40 CFR 122-125)
Texas Natural Resources Conservation Commission Guidance
Edwards Aquifer Authority Act (Texas Special District Local Laws Code Chapter 8801)

engines.name: Water Rights Engine
engines.function: Analyze water rights ownership, allocation, and priority systems including prior appropriation doctrine, riparian rights, groundwater ownership, and the interaction of water rights with oil and gas mineral operations in Texas and western states.
doctrine_topics: prior appropriation doctrine and priority system
riparian rights and reasonable use doctrine
groundwater rule of capture in Texas
correlative rights doctrine for groundwater
water right appropriation permit applications (TCEQ)
water right transfers, amendments, and cancellation
interstate water compacts and obligations
water right valuation and market transactions
conjunctive use of surface and groundwater
water rights and mineral estate interaction

golden_queries.question: An oil company in the Permian Basin wants to secure 2 million barrels of freshwater per month for hydraulic fracturing operations. The nearest surface water source is a tributary of the Pecos River (fully appropriated), and the local groundwater conservation district has begun rationing permits. Analyze the water rights options and legal framework.
required_elements: Texas groundwater rule of capture application
GCD permitting authority under TWC Chapter 36
water purchase and transfer agreement options
failure_signals: no distinction between surface and groundwater rights

golden_queries.question: A landowner in the Edwards Aquifer region discovers that a neighboring oil company is drilling a water well to supply fracking operations. The landowner's existing well has experienced declining water levels. Analyze the landowner's rights and remedies under Texas groundwater law.
required_elements: rule of capture limitations and exceptions
failure_signals: failure to address rule of capture
no remedy analysis for declining water levels

engines.name: Groundwater Analysis Engine
engines.function: Analyze groundwater resources, aquifer characteristics, well performance, groundwater contamination, and groundwater conservation district regulation as they relate to oil and gas operations and water supply.
doctrine_topics: aquifer characterization and hydrogeology fundamentals
groundwater well design, construction, and completion
aquifer testing and sustainable yield analysis
groundwater quality monitoring and standards
groundwater contamination source identification
groundwater conservation district desired future conditions
managed available groundwater (MAG) calculations
wellhead protection area delineation
aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) feasibility
groundwater modeling for resource assessment

golden_queries.question: Groundwater monitoring wells near a saltwater disposal facility show increasing chloride concentrations from 50 mg/L to 2,500 mg/L over 18 months. The Ogallala Aquifer underlies the area, and domestic water wells are within 1 mile. Analyze the contamination pathway, regulatory response, and operator liability.
failure_signals: failure to reference water quality standards

engines.name: Surface Water Permits Engine
engines.function: Analyze surface water appropriation permits, discharge permits, stormwater permits, and water quality certifications required for oil and gas operations, construction activities, and industrial facilities.
doctrine_topics: surface water appropriation permit requirements (TWC Chapter 11)
TPDES/NPDES discharge permit application and compliance
stormwater construction general permit (CGP/TXR150000)
multi-sector general permit for industrial facilities
Section 401 water quality certification
Section 404 wetlands fill permit coordination
total maximum daily load (TMDL) compliance
effluent limitation guidelines for oil and gas
zero discharge requirements for E&P operations
water quality standards and designated use protection

golden_queries.question: An oil company is constructing a 200-acre well pad and tank battery facility adjacent to a creek that feeds a public water supply reservoir. The project requires land clearing, road construction, and installation of a stormwater drainage system. Identify all required water-related permits and analyze the zero-discharge requirements for produced water.
required_elements: zero discharge for oil and gas produced water (40 CFR 435)
failure_signals: missing public water supply protection discussion

engines.name: Water Quality Engine
engines.function: Analyze water quality monitoring, standards, and compliance for both surface water and groundwater in the context of oil and gas operations including baseline testing, impact monitoring, and contamination response.
doctrine_topics: water quality standards and designated uses
baseline water quality testing protocols
impact monitoring well network design
drinking water maximum contaminant levels (MCLs)
oil and gas specific contaminant analysis (BTEX, TDS, chloride)
water quality data interpretation and trend analysis
stray gas migration detection and attribution
water quality complaint investigation protocols
remediation standard selection (risk-based vs background)
water quality reporting and notification requirements

golden_queries.question: A homeowner near a horizontal drilling operation reports that their well water has turned brown and has a petroleum odor. Pre-drill baseline water testing was conducted 6 months ago and showed no contamination. Analyze the investigation protocol, attribution methodology, and the operator's legal exposure.
required_elements: stray gas vs produced water contamination distinction
operator liability framework under Texas law

engines.name: Produced Water Engine
engines.function: Analyze produced water management including treatment, recycling, disposal, and beneficial reuse options for oil and gas operations. Evaluate regulatory requirements, economics, and emerging technologies for produced water handling.
doctrine_topics: produced water characterization and composition
produced water treatment technologies (membrane, evaporation, electrocoagulation)
produced water recycling for hydraulic fracturing
beneficial reuse regulations and opportunities
produced water disposal economics and logistics
produced water volume forecasting and management
seismicity concerns from produced water disposal
produced water transportation and transfer regulations
produced water handling facility permitting
produced water spill prevention and response

golden_queries.question: An operator in the Delaware Basin produces 50,000 barrels of water per day across 200 wells. Current disposal costs are $0.75/bbl via SWD wells. The nearest available SWD capacity is 30 miles away, and the RRC has paused new SWD permits in the area due to seismicity concerns. Analyze the produced water management alternatives and economics.
required_elements: recycling for frac reuse feasibility and cost
treatment technology comparison for TDS levels

engines.name: Injection Well Engine
engines.function: Analyze underground injection well permitting, operation, and compliance for saltwater disposal wells, enhanced recovery injection, and waste disposal wells under EPA UIC and Railroad Commission of Texas regulations.
doctrine_topics: UIC Class II well permit application (disposal and enhanced recovery)
RRC saltwater disposal well permitting (Rule 9)
injection well mechanical integrity testing (MIT)
area of review (AOR) analysis and corrective action
injection pressure and volume limitations
induced seismicity monitoring and response protocols
injection well monitoring and reporting requirements
well construction standards for injection wells
plugging and abandonment of injection wells
injection well financial assurance requirements

golden_queries.question: An operator wants to convert a depleted producing well to a saltwater disposal well in an area where 3 earthquakes above magnitude 3.0 have been recorded in the past year within 10 miles. The target injection zone is the Ellenburger formation at 12,000 feet. Analyze the permitting requirements, seismicity protocol compliance, and operational restrictions.
required_elements: RRC disposal well permit requirements (Form W-14)
seismic review trigger zones and restrictions
disposal volume and pressure limitations in seismic areas
